_README: Colloquial -> code vocabulary query expansion for the Building & Inspections
assistant.
WHY THIS EXISTS. Homeowners ask 'do I need a permit for a shed', not 'is a
detached accessory structure exempt from permit requirements'. Measured in the
sibling clerk project 2026-08-03: citizen phrasing pushed the governing provision
from rank 1 down to rank 10-19. The counter is exactly where plain language
arrives.
HOW IT WORKS. When a key phrase appears in the question, its code terms are
appended to the query token list before BM25 scoring. The resident's own words are
always kept — expansion only ADDS signal.
MAINTENANCE. Add a key whenever staff notice a question the assistant handles
poorly in plain language but well in code language. Only use terms that genuinely
appear in the corpus.
⚠ DO NOT add expansions for things this corpus cannot answer. ICC model codes are
COPYRIGHTED and adopted by reference — the corpus holds Michigan's AMENDMENT rules
but not the underlying code text. Zoning (setbacks, lot coverage, use) is a
different body of law entirely and is not here. Expanding toward material that
does not exist converts an honest refusal into a confident wrong answer, which is
the worst outcome this project can produce.
GOTCHA (learned in the clerk project): keys must disambiguate INTENT. A key that
matches two different kinds of question will poison one of them.
